newsitem.title: USA: U.S. trucking group fears soaring diesel prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. trucking group fears soaring diesel prices.

text.p: U.S. truckers on Tuesday raised concern that diesel prices might soar this winter because distillate stocks, used for heating oil and diesel, were very low and crude oil prices were high.
"Tight fuel supplies and Middle East tensions add up to trouble for truckers," said Thomas Donohue, president of the American Trucking Associations (ATA).
Average diesel fuel prices as of last week were 13 cents a gallon higher than a year ago, and in California they were 16 cents higher than the national average, ATA said.
Conditions this year are "even more alarming" than last winter, when diesel prices jumped more than 17 cents gallon in 10 weeks, Donohue said in a statement.
"Motor carriers are still struggling to absorb the fuel price increases that have occurred to date, let alone what may hit in the next few weeks," he said.

His statement came the day after the U.S. Energy Information Administration warned that heating oil and diesel prices were primed to rise because distillate stocks at the end of August were 16 percent lower than the five-year average for this time of year.
